key_insight: Scaling test-time verification (larger/faster verifier models or more verification compute) reduces the intention–action gap in vision-language-action tasks more effectively than proportionally scaling the policy/model that generates actions. A measured test-time scaling law shows verification yields stronger alignment gains per compute than policy scaling.
problem_solved: Reduces misalignment between natural-language instructions and generated robot actions (the "intention–action gap") without repeatedly retraining large policy models.
method: Characterize a test-time scaling law for embodied instruction following to quantify how verification performance improves with verifier capacity/compute.
Generate multiple candidate action trajectories from the policy at test time and apply a separately scaled verifier to score or filter candidates for instruction alignment.
Empirically compare scaling verification vs. scaling policy learning on embodied benchmarks to show verification offers better alignment-to-compute tradeoffs.
impact: Provides a practical, cost-effective strategy for improving instruction-following reliability in deployed VLA systems by investing in verification at test time rather than expensive policy retraining, improving safety and sample-efficiency for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: policy generates multiple candidate actions → verifier scores/ranks → selected aligned action executed.
Scaling-law chart: x-axis = verification/policy compute or model size, y-axis = alignment accuracy; show steeper gains for verification.
Bar/violin plots: comparative performance of (scaled policy) vs (scaled verifier) across benchmarks.
Icon set: robot + speech bubble, checklist/checkmark for verification, clock/compute meter to indicate test-time compute tradeoffs.
paper_title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment
paper_authors: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini
